html:
SMTO-GML-0058 — This Gmail request was too large to handle at once

GUID: 34807dfc-2be7-5574-85f4-c0882527f602
Slug: gmail-imap-data-limit
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • The search results, email thread, attachment, or data passed between SMTO and the Gateway was bigger than SMTO allows, or didn't arrive complete. SMTO stopped rather than use partial mail.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Narrow the request, for example by adding a sender, a date range, or a subject, or ask SMTO for fewer messages at once. Very large searches and long threads go past what SMTO can read safely in one request.
  2. If you're sending a large attachment, use a smaller file or split the files across several emails. Each email and each transfer to the Gateway has a size limit.
  3. If the request was sending or changing mail, check Sent, Drafts, and the affected messages in Gmail before asking again. A transfer can fail after Gmail already accepted part of the change.
  4. If several large Gmail requests are running at the same time, let them finish before you start another one. The Gateway can only hold a limited amount of mail data at once, shared by all running requests.

What success looks like

  • The smaller request returns results, or the email is sent and appears once in Sent.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a send until you've checked Sent, and don't switch to another account to get around the limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Mailbox data exceeded a read allowance (25 MiB per message, 40 MiB per fetch, 50,000 search matches, thread size), the Gateway transfer store hit capacity (100 handles, 96 MiB, 100,000 rows), or a staged transfer failed size, order or SHA-256 checks.

What this means

  • Mailbox data exceeded a bounded read or staging allowance, or a private transfer failed integrity checks. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: Mailbox data exceeded a bounded read or staging allowance, or a private transfer failed integrity checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Narrow the query (sender, date, label), lower max_results, read fewer messages or choose a smaller attachment. For an interrupted write, inspect the receipt and Gmail state before any further action; transfer tickets expire after ten minutes or on Gateway restart, so expired data must be fetched again with a new read.
  • Narrow the search, read fewer messages, or choose a smaller attachment. For an interrupted write, inspect the receipt and Gmail state before taking further action. Expired transfer data must be fetched again through a new read.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
